The resolution step now uses the cleaning work more consistently: extracted aliases help generate and accept matches, and explicit `Trade Union` records containing “Unite” can resolve across their name variants. HSBC’s differently spelled records now group when their extracted names and normalized addresses support the match. Source spellings and payment attributions remain intact; the displayed name uses the most commonly reported spelling.

I also added a real clean-to-resolve CLI regression test: Carlton Club and Carlton Club Political Committee share an address, but stay separate and are surfaced for review. That guards against solving missed matches by merging too broadly.

The end-to-end test passed with real Splink, the 72 Rust library tests passed, and all 6 Python worker tests passed. Strict Clippy still reports existing issues in unrelated loading code. The changes are committed on branch `feat/looser-funder-resolution-20261008` in worktree `/Users/jamie/development/exposed-declaration-loader-fix-20261008`.

This follows the pstack principles of modeling evidence explicitly, addressing the cause in both candidate generation and match acceptance, and testing observable resolution behavior.

PR #27 is open against `main`: [Use extracted evidence in funder resolution](https://github.com/johnnylarner/exposed/pull/27).

It includes the HSBC and Unite resolution changes, the Carlton Club false-merge regression test, and the validation results.

content.text:
Use PR branch from repo root. Ensure `.env` has `DATABASE_URL` and PostgreSQL is running (`make db-start`).

```sh
python3 -m venv resolution/.venv
resolution/.venv/bin/python -m pip install ./resolution

ingestion_key=$(uuidgen)
cargo run --package exposed --bin exposed -- data declarations fetch exposed/config/declarations-dev.yaml --ingestion-key "$ingestion_key"
cargo run --package exposed --bin exposed -- data declarations clean exposed/config/declarations-dev.yaml --ingestion-key "$ingestion_key"
cargo run --package exposed --bin exposed -- data declarations resolve exposed/config/declaration-resolution-dev.yaml --ingestion-key "$ingestion_key"
cargo run --package exposed --bin exposed -- data declarations load exposed/config/declarations-dev.yaml --ingestion-key "$ingestion_key"
```

Stored members must already exist. Fetch captures their declarations with fresh `fetched_at` values. Clean and resolve refuse existing output directories. Load requires raw, cleaned, and resolved artifacts together. It atomically replaces declarations/payments only when capture timestamps are newer.

Already-loaded ingestion keys cannot be re-resolved and loaded again. Different artifacts cause a fingerprint conflict; identical retries are no-ops. Copying old raw data to a new key does not bypass the equal/newer timestamp guard.

Important limitation for root response: loading the new run updates payment attribution but does **not** remove old unused funder rows, and search includes those rows. Therefore these commands alone may leave earlier HSBC/Unite duplicates visible. This is code evidence from `exposed/src/lib/outbound/declaration_loading.rs` (insert/upsert funders, only deletes funding entries) and `exposed/src/lib/outbound/funder.rs` (searches all funders). Do not promise the UI duplicate list disappears.

Config uses `data_dir: ./exposed/data`, `resolution_python: resolution/.venv/bin/python`, `resolution_worker: resolution/worker.py`, candidate budget 1,000,000. CLI loads `.env` automatically. No DB connection runtime needed for clean or resolve, although Cargo SQLx compilation needs `DATABASE_URL` or query cache.

Existing unimported runs can reuse their key for clean → resolve → load. Already-cleaned but unresolved runs need only resolve → load. Existing resolved bundle must be backed up/moved before resolve will rerun, and this is useful only offline or before first load.
